NUTRITION
  GUIDELINES:
    - "Daily calorie target: moderate deficit ~ 300-500 kcal below estimated maintenance. Reassess in 4 weeks."
    - "Protein: 1.2-1.6 g/kg bodyweight per day (prioritise protein at each meal). Increase protein slightly on high-intensity days to support recovery."
    - "Carbohydrate distribution: prioritise carbohydrates around exercise (pre- and post-workout) to reduce postprandial glycaemia. Increase peri-workout carbs modestly on high-intensity Phase 3 days to support performance and avoid hypoglycaemia."
    - "Fasted cardio: if performing fasted morning cardio, ensure she is clinically stable on metformin, monitor for hypoglycaemia, limit session duration to 20-40 minutes of low-to-moderate intensity, and carry fast-acting carbohydrate."
    - "Pre-workout for fasted cardio: prefer remaining fasted; if symptomatic or for high-intensity sessions, use a small snack ~15-25 g carbs + 10-15 g protein 20-60 minutes prior."
    - "Post-workout snacks: aim for ~20-30 g carbohydrate + 15-25 g protein within 30-60 minutes after exercise. Examples: low-fat Greek yogurt + banana; protein shake + apple; cottage cheese + oats; wholegrain toast + cottage cheese."
    - "Fats: remaining calories from healthy fats (olive oil, nuts, oily fish)."
    - "Fiber: aim for 25-35 g/day from whole grains, legumes, vegetables."
    - "Meal timing: regular meals every 3-4 hours to reduce glycaemic variability. After fasted cardio or high-intensity sessions, prioritise a meal/snack with carbohydrate+protein within 30-60 minutes."
    - "Intermittent fasting: can be considered after medical clearance. Prefer conservative approaches (12:12 or 14:10) and avoid aggressive fasting if hypoglycaemia risk or using hypoglycaemia-causing meds."
    - "Cheat meal policy: allow one planned weekly higher-calorie meal; prefer timing after a training session, include protein and some carbohydrate, limit excess alcohol, and monitor capillary glucose 1-2 hours post-meal."
    - "Avoid very low carbohydrate extremes unless supervised by her clinician; maintain consistent carbohydrate intake and monitor glucose."
    - "Hydration: at least 1.5-2 L/day; more on training and high-intensity days."
    - "Medication consideration: continue metformin; advise client to discuss any significant dietary change, IF adoption, or hypoglycaemia symptoms with prescribing clinician. If on other glucose-lowering meds that increase hypoglycaemia risk, increase monitoring and liaise with clinician before Phase 3 intensity increases."

  SAMPLE_DAY:
    - "Breakfast: Greek yogurt or cottage cheese, oats, berries, 20-30 g protein (or small pre-workout snack before high-intensity sessions)."
    - "Snack: small apple + 10-15 g nuts or 1 boiled egg."
    - "Lunch: grilled lean protein, large mixed salad, quinoa or wholegrain bread portion."
    - "Pre-workout: for fasted cardio skip pre-exercise snack unless symptomatic. For high-intensity Phase 3 sessions consider 1 small snack (e.g. low-fat yogurt + banana) 20-60 minutes prior."
    - "Post-workout: protein shake + fruit or wholegrain toast with cottage cheese within 30-60 minutes."
    - "Dinner: salmon or chicken, mixed vegetables, sweet potato or brown rice."
    - "Cheat meal (once weekly): planned higher-calorie meal; include protein and carbohydrate, limit excess alcohol, and monitor glucose 1-2 hours after."
    - "Evening snack (if needed): cottage cheese or 1 serving of nuts."

  MONITORING:
    - "Weekly: body weight, training adherence, weekly steps (aim +3000 steps/week above baseline)."
    - "Every 4 weeks: review energy intake, adjust calories if weight loss <0.5 kg/week after initial 2 weeks."
    - "Glycaemic monitoring: check capillary glucose as advised by clinician; measure fasting and postprandial trends, and pre/post-exercise (especially around fasted cardio and higher intensity Phase 3 sessions). Monitor glucose 1-2 hours after cheat meals for several instances."
    - "During IF trial: monitor fasting, pre/post-exercise, and postprandial glucose more frequently for first 2-4 weeks."
    - "Monitor recovery markers (sleep, perceived soreness, energy) during Phase 3; reduce intensity if poor recovery."
    - "Referral: coordinate with client's GP/endocrinologist for HbA1c monitoring and medication review if weight loss or changes in intake/activity occur."

SAFETY
  CONSIDERATIONS:
    - "Avoid high-impact plyometrics if there are joint issues; substituted with low-impact alternatives."
    - "Fasted cardio precautions: limit duration and intensity when fasted, monitor for hypoglycaemia signs (dizziness, sweating, confusion). Carry fast-acting carbohydrate during sessions and stop if symptomatic."
    - "Increased intensity precautions: progress load and intensity gradually; prioritise technique and joint-friendly variations. Consider reducing fasted cardio frequency on weeks with high-intensity resistance sessions."
    - "Cheat meal safety: choose a single planned meal rather than frequent large binges. Monitor glucose and symptoms after cheat meals; if large glucose excursions or hypoglycaemia occur, reduce frequency or size and liaise with clinician/dietitian."
    - "Intermittent fasting caution: get medical clearance before starting IF; avoid IF if on hypoglycaemia-causing medications without specialist supervision."
    - "If any cardiovascular symptoms, stop exercise and seek medical review."
    - "Encourage appropriate footwear and exercise selection for joint health."

VISIT_FREQUENCY "12 weeks plan with 3 gym sessions/week; nutrition review every 2-4 weeks; review fasted cardio/IF tolerance after 1-2 weeks; review cheat meal response after 2-4 weeks"

NUTRITION
  GUIDELINES:
    - "Daily calorie target: moderate deficit ~ 300-500 kcal below estimated maintenance. Reassess in 4 weeks."
    - "Protein: 1.2-1.6 g/kg bodyweight per day (prioritise protein at each meal). Increase protein slightly on high-intensity days to support recovery."
    - "Carbohydrate distribution: prioritise carbohydrates around exercise (pre- and post-workout) to reduce postprandial glycaemia. Increase peri-workout carbs modestly on high-intensity Phase 3 days to support performance and avoid hypoglycaemia."
    - "Fasted cardio: if performing fasted morning cardio, ensure she is clinically stable on metformin, monitor for hypoglycaemia, limit session duration to 20-40 minutes of low-to-moderate intensity, and carry fast-acting carbohydrate."
    - "Pre-workout for fasted cardio: prefer remaining fasted; if symptomatic or for high-intensity sessions, use a small snack ~15-25 g carbs + 10-15 g protein 20-60 minutes prior."
    - "Post-workout snacks: aim for ~20-30 g carbohydrate + 15-25 g protein within 30-60 minutes after exercise. Examples: low-fat Greek yogurt + banana; protein shake + apple; cottage cheese + oats; wholegrain toast + cottage cheese."
    - "Fats: remaining calories from healthy fats (olive oil, nuts, oily fish)."
    - "Fiber: aim for 25-35 g/day from whole grains, legumes, vegetables."
    - "Meal timing: regular meals every 3-4 hours to reduce glycaemic variability. After fasted cardio or high-intensity sessions, prioritise a meal/snack with carbohydrate+protein within 30-60 minutes."
    - "Intermittent fasting: can be considered after medical clearance. Prefer conservative approaches (12:12 or 14:10) and avoid aggressive fasting if hypoglycaemia risk or using hypoglycaemia-causing meds."
    - "Cheat meal policy: allow one planned weekly higher-calorie meal; prefer timing after a training session, include protein and some carbohydrate, limit excess alcohol, and monitor capillary glucose 1-2 hours post-meal."
    - "Avoid very low carbohydrate extremes unless supervised by her clinician; maintain consistent carbohydrate intake and monitor glucose."
    - "Hydration: at least 1.5-2 L/day; more on training and high-intensity days."
    - "Medication consideration: continue metformin; advise client to discuss any significant dietary change, IF adoption, or hypoglycaemia symptoms with prescribing clinician. If on other glucose-lowering meds that increase hypoglycaemia risk, increase monitoring and liaise with clinician before Phase 3 intensity increases."

  SAMPLE_DAY:
    - "Breakfast: Greek yogurt or cottage cheese, oats, berries, 20-30 g protein (or small pre-workout snack before high-intensity sessions)."
    - "Snack: small apple + 10-15 g nuts or 1 boiled egg."
    - "Lunch: grilled lean protein, large mixed salad, quinoa or wholegrain bread portion."
    - "Pre-workout: for fasted cardio skip pre-exercise snack unless symptomatic. For high-intensity Phase 3 sessions consider 1 small snack (e.g. low-fat yogurt + banana) 20-60 minutes prior."
    - "Post-workout: protein shake + fruit or wholegrain toast with cottage cheese within 30-60 minutes."
    - "Dinner: salmon or chicken, mixed vegetables, sweet potato or brown rice."
    - "Cheat meal (once weekly): planned higher-calorie meal; include protein and carbohydrate, limit excess alcohol, and monitor glucose 1-2 hours after."
    - "Evening snack (if needed): cottage cheese or 1 serving of nuts."

  MONITORING:
    - "Weekly: body weight, training adherence, weekly steps (aim +3000 steps/week above baseline)."
    - "Every 4 weeks: review energy intake, adjust calories if weight loss <0.5 kg/week after initial 2 weeks."
    - "Glycaemic monitoring: check capillary glucose as advised by clinician; measure fasting and postprandial trends, and pre/post-exercise (especially around fasted cardio and higher intensity Phase 3 sessions). Monitor glucose 1-2 hours after cheat meals for several instances."
    - "During IF trial: monitor fasting, pre/post-exercise, and postprandial glucose more frequently for first 2-4 weeks."
    - "Monitor recovery markers (sleep, perceived soreness, energy) during Phase 3; reduce intensity if poor recovery."
    - "Referral: coordinate with client's GP/endocrinologist for HbA1c monitoring and medication review if weight loss or changes in intake/activity occur."

SAFETY
  CONSIDERATIONS:
    - "Avoid high-impact plyometrics if there are joint issues; substituted with low-impact alternatives."
    - "Fasted cardio precautions: limit duration and intensity when fasted, monitor for hypoglycaemia signs (dizziness, sweating, confusion). Carry fast-acting carbohydrate during sessions and stop if symptomatic."
    - "Increased intensity precautions: progress load and intensity gradually; prioritise technique and joint-friendly variations. Consider reducing fasted cardio frequency on weeks with high-intensity resistance sessions."
    - "Cheat meal safety: choose a single planned meal rather than frequent large binges. Monitor glucose and symptoms after cheat meals; if large glucose excursions or hypoglycaemia occur, reduce frequency or size and liaise with clinician/dietitian."
    - "Intermittent fasting caution: get medical clearance before starting IF; avoid IF if on hypoglycaemia-causing medications without specialist supervision."
    - "If any cardiovascular symptoms, stop exercise and seek medical review."
    - "Encourage appropriate footwear and exercise selection for joint health."
